title: Chat — Direct message — payload
description: One person writes, rewrites or withdraws a message, or a reaction, in their direct conversation with another. A message is named by its author-minted `messageId` and carries its whole content on every revision; the author edits it by sending the same `messageId` with a greater `revision` and an `editedAt`, withdraws it by sending a rewrite with an empty `body`, and reacts to another message with a message of `kind: reaction` whose `body` is the reaction's value. The content vocabulary is the rooms one (`rooms/_shared/0.1`, `SealedRecordBody`). The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

kind.description: What a reader shows the message as: `message`, a turn in the conversation, or `reaction`, a short response to another message. REQUIRED here, where rooms makes it optional only for readers that predate it. An open set: a reader MUST present a kind it does not know as rooms says (as a note, its `body` inert) and MUST NOT refuse a document for its kind. A rewrite MUST keep it.

inReplyTo.description: OPTIONAL on a `message`: the message this one answers. REQUIRED on a `reaction`: the message it responds to, which a rewrite of the reaction MUST keep.

writtenAt.description: The instant the author wrote the message, RFC 3339 in UTC (`Z`). REQUIRED. Set on revision 1 and carried unchanged on every rewrite; what marks an edit is `editedAt`. The author's claim: a reader orders the conversation by it and treats an implausible or backdated one as the specification's *Ordering in the conversation* says.

editedAt.description: The instant the author made the edit that produced this revision, RFC 3339 in UTC (`Z`). Absent on revision 1 and REQUIRED on every later revision, so a reader seeing a message for the first time can tell whether it was edited. Display only: it never orders rewrites.

oneOf.description: The first revision of a message or reaction: `revision` 1, a non-empty `body`, no `editedAt`, and a reaction names its target in `inReplyTo`.
A rewrite (an edit, a withdrawal, a changed or withdrawn reaction): `revision` greater than 1, `editedAt` present, and a reaction names its target in `inReplyTo`.
